transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, doctor. Well, I'm here because... the medical clinic for this logistics job I applied for wouldn't clear me. They told me my weight was too low. 

I don't really see it, honestly. To me, I just look lean, you know? Just like a guy who's ready to work and stay quick on his feet on the floor. But they made a big deal out of it and said I needed to be evaluated, so here I am.
Have you been deliberately eating less food than you used to, or doing things to keep your weight down?

Well, yeah, I suppose I do eat less than I used to. Most days I just keep it to black coffee... maybe a boiled egg or a little tuna. That's really about it. 

And if I'm not working—like if I'm not moving freight on a shift—I just tell myself I don't need a real meal anyway. I'm not burning the energy, so there's no point in eating a bunch of food. So, yeah, I guess I do keep it pretty strict.
When you look at yourself in the mirror or think about your body, do you feel like you're overweight or too heavy?

Well, I wouldn't use the word overweight, exactly. But... when I look in the mirror, especially at my stomach and my waist, I do feel like I need to be smaller. 

If I'm not tight-looking in those areas, it bothers me. It makes me feel like... well, like if I let that go, then I'm not the disciplined man I used to be out on the warehouse floor. So I just focus on keeping it tight.
Besides eating less, do you do anything else to try to prevent weight gain—like exercising a lot, using laxatives, or making yourself vomit?

No, I... I don't do any of that stuff. I definitely don't take laxatives or make myself sick, nothing like that. 

And as for exercise, well, moving freight and stock around all day is plenty of a workout on its own, you know? It's heavy work. So I don't go out of my way to run or hit a gym after a shift. I really just stick to keeping my food intake low, like I mentioned. That's about it.
Do you ever have times when you eat a large amount of food in a short period of time—like you lose control and eat much more than you planned to?

No, I don't do that. I never really have times where I just eat a whole bunch of food at once. 

Honestly, I don't think I could even stomach a large amount of food right now if I tried. Like I was saying, I keep things pretty strictly controlled, so... no, losing control and eating like that just isn't something that happens with me.
How long have you been eating this restrictively—keeping your food intake to just coffee, an egg, and maybe some tuna? Has it been weeks, months, or longer?

I'm not exactly sure, to be honest. I haven't really kept track of the weeks or months. 

It's just... it's been a while. It kind of just became my normal routine over time, so I couldn't give you a specific date or timeframe for when it started getting this strict. I just know it's been my normal for a bit now.
What is your current weight, and how tall are you? Also, do you remember what you weighed before you started eating more restrictively?

I'm about 5 foot 10. As for my weight, well... they weighed me at the clinic the other day and it was around 112 pounds. I think I used to be closer to 165 or 170 before I started cutting back, but I'm not entirely sure. 

Honestly, the main reason I'm even here talking to you is because the medical clinic for my logistics job said my weight was too low to clear me. They wouldn't sign off on my physical for work. I don't really get it, because to me, I just look lean. I just look like someone who's ready to work and can stay quick on his feet, you know?

Besides the weight loss and the clinic's concern, have you noticed any other changes in your body—like feeling cold all the time, your hair thinning, your period stopping if you menstruate, or feeling dizzy or faint?

No, not really. I mean, I don't get periods, obviously. But as for the rest of it... no. I don't feel dizzy or faint, and I haven't noticed my hair thinning out or anything like that. I guess I get cold sometimes, but it's winter, so that just seems normal to me. I feel fine, honestly.
